title: Mortality among people with regular or problematic use of amphetamines: A systematic review and meta-analysis

claims.statement: In cohorts of people with regular or problematic amphetamine use (25 cohorts, mostly people in treatment, people who inject drugs or people with hospital diagnoses), all-cause mortality was 1.11 deaths per 100 person-years (95% CI 0.90–1.37), 6.83 times (5.27–8.84) that of the general population of the same age and sex; standardized ratios were highest for drug poisoning (24.7), suicide (12.2) and homicide (11.9). Heterogeneity was very high (I² 97–98%), and ratios for 13 cohorts were imputed by the reviewers.
claims.magnitude: Crude 1.11 per 100 person-years (0.90–1.37); SMR 6.83 (5.27–8.84); 5.71 (4.44–7.35) in the 8 cohorts reporting their own SMR. Cause-specific SMR: drug poisoning 24.70 (16.67–36.58), suicide 12.20 (4.89–30.47), homicide 11.90 (7.82–18.12), cardiovascular 5.12 (3.74–7.00), accidental injury 5.12 (2.88–9.08).
